exposure: risk adjustment in congenital heart surgery categories IV to VI
higher pre- and postsurgery respiratory support
delayed postsurgery enteral and oral feeding
higher pre- and postsurgery gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
cohort: The study included 128 infants under 6 months of age who underwent congenital heart disease surgery between 2016 and 2021.
finding: The prevalence of tube-feeding at discharge was 18.8%, and admission at birth, higher presurgery milk calories, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) were significant risk factors.
followup_time: Variable, up to hospital discharge (mean 72 days for TF vs 17 days for independent oral feeding)
birth_weight: N/A (low birth weight was an identified risk factor, but not a defining characteristic for the entire cohort)
